# Experimental setup

**Model stack.** Primary results use pretrained `google/gemma-3-270m` with
Gemma Scope~2 PT CLT `width_262k_l0_medium_affine` and the `nnsight`
backend [@gemma3; @gemmascope2]. We prefer pretrained+affine over
instruction-tuned stacks for this task: Appendix~J of @hanna2026latent
finds base models slightly stronger on \(a\)/\(an\), and Hub IT
`medium_affine` layer~0 was unavailable in our setup. All reported
feature IDs are for the PT+affine stack. This model strongly prefers
majority \(a\) and sits below the scale regime where @hanna2026latent
report reliable behavioral planning success; we therefore focus on
*editable* mechanisms and assay validation rather than behavioral demos.

**Task.** Latent-Planning-style occupation prompts of the form
``Someone who \ldots\ is'' with a fixed one-shot demonstration.
Early mismatch discovery and the held-out transfer that first broke a
wrapper reading are summarized in Appendix~A; the main text starts from
free-generation package-like assays and fixed-article controls.

**Feature families.** From attribution graphs on eight selection
occupations (disjoint from the free-generation test set) we construct
\(k{=}4\) feature sets: **S1** dual-effect (positive direct effect on
`an` *and* on the future noun); **S2** article-ish (positive on `an`,
near-zero on future content); **S3** content-ish (positive on future
content, near-zero on `an`); **S4** competing / `a`-favoring.
Activation-matched random controls match mean activation of the
intervened set. Later assays add **per-noun** Latent-Planning-style
features for a same-class target with low \(|\mathrm{attr}(a/an)|\), and
hint-contrast sets. Default free-generation interventions amplify
\(5\times\) prompt-specific activation at \(P\); dose sweeps use
\(\{1.5,2,3,5,8\}\times\). Large multiplicative gains can be
off-manifold; our central factorial therefore evaluates the *same* S1
handle on and off under identical token prefixes rather than generalizing
from unrelated handles.

**Synthetic method check.** Before interpreting Gemma residuals, we run the
same estimands on two ground-truth autoregressive mechanisms with eight
occupation cues: a mediated article-only mechanism and a direct persistent-plan
mechanism. Acceptance requires near-zero token-clamped residual control for
the mediated model and large force-`a` residual TV (\(\ge 0.40\)) with a
non-collapsing \(k\)-curve for the direct model.

**Exact S1 factorial.** We evaluate all 20 held-out E1 prompts under S1
off/on crossed with free, forced-`a`, and forced-`an` generation. S1 uses
the four selection-only features at layers 10--13 and the pre-registered
\(5\times\) gain. Forced cells keep S1 active at \(P\) for noun prediction.
Recomputed attention is primary; `circuit-tracer`'s
`freeze_attention=True` path is reported separately. We store
full-vocabulary distances and top-50 distributions, while target metrics
cover pre-specified listed/twin nouns and teacher-forced multi-token nouns.

**Propagation and full-residual reference.** On four fixed prompts we
record sparse CLT activations at the forced-`an` position with S1 off/on.
As a sensitivity control, paired prompts share an occupation sentence and
differ only in an explicit source/target vocabulary cue; both use fixed
`a`. We patch the complete decoder-layer output residual at the article
position, choose the layer with largest mean target-specific
\(\Delta\Delta\) on four development pairs, and compare its effect on four
held-out pairs with ten matched-norm random directions. This intervention
tests whether upstream noun computation can move the target through the
same model stack; it does not claim semantic equivalence to S1.

**Held-out sets and uncertainty.** Free-generation package-like results use
\(N{=}20\) held-out occupations including seven pre-specified twin pairs.
The same 20 prompts define the primary factorial; the 19 prompts on which
the article changes are labeled descriptive. Full-residual layer selection
and evaluation use disjoint four-pair development/test splits.
Prompt-level and pair-level intervals use 10,000-sample nonparametric
bootstrap resampling. Full prompts, feature IDs, tokenization audits, and
machine-readable summaries are released in the accompanying code.
